# RAGGuard

> RAGGuard checks that a RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) index matches its source documents. It compares the files in Amazon S3 with a Qdrant or pgvector index, and optionally the ingestion pipeline's own records, and reports missing, stale, half-indexed, duplicate, empty, deleted-but-still-searchable and wrong-tenant chunks, with the evidence and a safe fix. It only reads your systems. Free during the beta.

RAGGuard is a hosted web app with an HTTP API, a command-line tool (`ragguard`) and an MCP server, so AI coding assistants can run its checks. It never writes to your storage or index: fixes go to your own worker as signed requests, and old vectors are removed only after you approve, unless you switch on automatic clean-up.

## Guides

- [Guides: keep your RAG index in sync with your source documents]({BASE}/guides): Eight silent ways a RAG index drifts away from its source documents, with a copy-paste check for each: SQL for pgvector, and the same idea for Qdrant.
- [Find documents missing from your vector index]({BASE}/guides/find-documents-missing-from-your-vector-index): A file can sit in your bucket while nothing about it is searchable. Compare the documents in storage with the documents in your index to find them.
- [Detect stale embeddings after a document changes]({BASE}/guides/detect-stale-embeddings-after-a-document-changes): When a source file changes but its chunks do not, your RAG app keeps answering from the old version. Store the file's hash on every chunk and compare.
- [Find documents with two versions in the index]({BASE}/guides/find-documents-with-two-versions-in-the-index): The new version of a document was indexed, but the old chunks were never deleted, so both versions answer questions. Count the distinct versions per document.
- [Make sure deleted documents are not still searchable]({BASE}/guides/make-sure-deleted-documents-are-not-still-searchable): Deleting a file from storage does not delete its vectors. Find chunks whose source file no longer exists, then prove whether a search can still return them.
- [Find half-indexed documents]({BASE}/guides/find-half-indexed-documents): An ingestion worker can die after writing only some of a document's chunks. Store the expected chunk count on every chunk and look for gaps.
- [Find duplicate chunks from retried ingestion]({BASE}/guides/find-duplicate-chunks-from-retried-ingestion): A retried ingestion job can write the same chunk twice. Duplicates crowd other content out of the top results and skew answers. Group by document and position to find them.
- [Find empty or all-zero vectors]({BASE}/guides/find-empty-or-all-zero-vectors): A failed embedding call can leave a chunk with no vector or a vector of zeros. Such a chunk can never be found by search. Check the vector's length.
- [Catch chunks tagged with the wrong tenant]({BASE}/guides/catch-chunks-tagged-with-the-wrong-tenant): In a multi-tenant RAG app, one chunk with the wrong tenant tag can show one customer's content to another. Compare every chunk's tenant with its source file's tenant.
- [Use RAGGuard from your AI assistant]({BASE}/guides/use-ragguard-from-your-ai-assistant): Let Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or any MCP-capable assistant check your RAG index for you: a rule to paste into your project, an MCP server, and a command your assistant can run.
